Curriculum at a Glance
At Light Years School, our curriculum is designed to be both inspiring and carefully structured. Each half term is built around an engaging “Curriculum Connection Driver” – a central topic that brings learning together and helps children make meaningful links across subjects.
Our curriculum follows an interconnected approach, where knowledge is deliberately sequenced and revisited to support children in building secure understanding over time. This ensures that learning is cumulative, coherent, and enables pupils to know more, remember more, and do more. We are guided by the principle that clear curricular alignment is essential to provide purpose, vision and direction (Turner, 2023), and this underpins all aspects of our curriculum design.
Through our carefully planned topics, we aim to ensure that all pupils understand the purpose of their learning. Our curriculum is designed to spark curiosity, develop rich knowledge and skills, and inspire children through engaging and memorable learning experiences. As a result, pupils are supported to make strong connections, deepen their understanding, and achieve ambitious outcomes.
The school’s curriculum is highly ambitious and carefully shaped around pupils’ needs and interests. A focus on holistic development does not detract from the broad and detailed subject curriculum that pupils experience.
Ofsted Report June 2024.

pageCache.text:
Reporting and Requesting Absences
At Light Years School we want all children to have a positive experience of school life and be able to reach their full potential. One way in which parents can help their child to do this is by ensuring they attend school every day.
We do recognise that there will be times that your child will not be able to attend school. If your child is unwell and unable to attend, it is the responsibility of you as a parent/carer to inform the school. A telephone call to the office on 01329 760955 before 9am is necessary; otherwise an unauthorised absence will be recorded. ​In the event of your child having a medical appointment during school time, please inform the school office providing evidence of the appointment. We will follow up on any absences not reported in line with our attendance policies and safeguarding policies.
NHS Guidance - Is my child too ill for school?
Absence Requests
If a parent/carer wishes to take their child out of school for any reason, this must be requested via a absence request form to Sarah Alden, Headteacher.
Holidays during term time will not be granted unless they are considered to be 'exceptional circumstances'.
The school considers each application for term-time absence individually, taking into account the specific facts, circumstances and relevant context behind the request. A leave of absence is granted entirely at the Headteachers discretion.

Pupil Premium Information
Well-being is another sustained focus at Light Years School. We understand the importance of mental health in facilitating effective learning, and we incorporate this into our daily practices. Our commitment to overcoming challenges related to poor working memory is achieved through retrieval practices and a multi-sensory approach to teaching, which engages students on various levels.
In addition to academic support, we embed personal development throughout our curriculum, broadening life experiences and fostering essential skills for the future. Under the guidance of our Pupil Premium Lead, Emily Smart, we continually strive to enhance our offer, ensuring that Pupil Premium funding is effectively used to promote equity in educational opportunities for all students.

Personal Development
At Light Years School, we believe that personal development is a fundamental aspect of a broad and balanced education.
In addition to our trips, we host an array of visitors, including pilots, guide dogs, and animals from Zoolab. These interactions not only enrich our curriculum but also broaden our students' horizons and enhance their understanding of diverse professions and lifestyles. By nurturing skills such as teamwork, resilience, and empathy, we are dedicated to developing confident individuals ready to face the challenges of tomorrow. At Light Years School, we strive to inspire and empower each student on their personal development journey.

Multi Sensory
At Light Years School, our multi-sensory approach is a defining strength of our provision and is embedded across every aspect of school life. It sets us apart and underpins how we enable all pupils to access, engage with and succeed in their learning.
Multi-sensory teaching means that children learn through a combination of visual, auditory, kinaesthetic and tactile experiences. Research consistently shows that learning is stronger when pupils are actively engaged through multiple pathways, as this supports memory, understanding and the ability to transfer skills over time. This approach is particularly effective for pupils with special educational needs, as it removes barriers and ensures that learning is accessible, meaningful and inclusive.
At Light Years, this is not an ‘add-on’ -it is our everyday practice. Every lesson is carefully designed to include opportunities for pupils to see, hear, say and do. Teachers use concrete resources, visuals, movement, structured talk and hands-on experiences to bring learning to life and support deep understanding. This consistent approach across the school ensures that pupils feel confident, know what to expect and are able to build on prior learning effectively.
We have worked in partnership with leading multi-sensory expert Dr Susie Nyman to develop and refine our approach. Through this collaboration, our staff are highly skilled in delivering evidence-informed teaching strategies that meet the diverse needs of our learners. Ongoing training and coaching ensure that high-quality multi-sensory teaching is sustained and continually developed.
Our commitment extends beyond the classroom. We provide carefully planned opportunities for sensory exploration throughout the school day, including a dedicated multi-sensory tuff tray available during outdoor and break times. These activities, often planned by our Thrive practitioners, support regulation, creativity and engagement, ensuring pupils are ready to learn.
The impact of this approach is clear: pupils are engaged, motivated and able to access learning in ways that work for them. They develop stronger understanding, increased independence and a positive attitude towards learning.
At Light Years School, multi-sensory learning is not just a strategy—it is a fundamental part of who we are. It reflects our commitment to research-informed practice and ensures that every child is supported to thrive.
Our Tuff Trays
Multi-sensory activities are available daily at break and lunchtimes. These are designed and created by Carrie-Ann, a member of the Inclusion Practitioner team. The pupils love to access these!

Vision and Values
At Light Years School our ethos is clear; we put the child first in all circumstances. To ensure our pupils are ready to learn, Light Years School has created a school environment which makes pupils feel safe, secure, and supported. We do this by establishing strong and trusted professional relationships and providing pupils with an inviting and accessible environment. By understanding our children and their journeys barriers to learning can be reduced or overcome.
​At Light Years School, we want our pupils to grow tall, be proud of their achievements and confidently enter the next phase of their education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Light Years School - Mental Health and Wellbeing
pageCache.text:
Mental Health and Wellbeing
Light Years School is committed to eliminating the prejudice and stigma associated with mental health needs by establishing a whole school approach to emotional health and mental wellbeing where mental health is promoted in a positive way rather than seen as a stigma.
Light Years School Mental Health and Wellbeing framework is based around four key elements:
Prevention: creating a safe and happy environment where mental health problems are less likely, improving mental health and wellbeing of the whole school population, and equipping pupils to be resilient so that they can manage the normal stress of life effectively. Teaching pupils about mental wellbeing through the curriculum and reinforcing this teaching through school activities and ethos.
Identification: recognising emerging issues as early and accurately as possible.
Early support: helping pupils/staff to access evidence based early support and interventions.
Access to specialist support: working effectively with external agencies to provide swift access or referrals to specialist support and treatment.
The Good Mental Health Handbook has been developed by Hampshire CAMHS and parents/carers. Within its pages, it contains information, short videos, and workshops to support our children's mental health challenges including anxiety, bereavement, depression, self-harm, eating disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorder, sexuality, substance misuse and trauma.
The Good Mental Health Handbook is a one-stop shop of practical resources, strategies and activities to help the whole family navigate some of the most delicate and sensitive issues facing families today.

SMSC
At Light Years School, we are deeply committed to fostering the holistic development of our pupils through a robust framework encompassing Spiritual, Moral, Social, and Cultural (SMSC) education. We believe that the development of the whole child is paramount, and we integrate SMSC principles throughout our teaching and school culture.
Our approach to SMSC is primarily delivered through our comprehensive PSHE and RE lessons, complemented by engaging assemblies and enriching whole school curriculum activities. These aspects are meticulously designed to nurture the personal development of each pupil, providing them with a strong foundation in understanding and respecting the fundamental British Values, such as democracy, individual liberty, the rule of law, and mutual respect.
The PSHE programme at Light Years School is carefully planned, ensuring that it addresses essential topics relevant to our students’ lives. We embed the Light Years Code throughout our school, which prioritises the opportunity for restorative conversations. This focus on oracy and 'using kind words' is crucial in creating a positive school culture where every child feels valued and understood. As well as this, we have embedded the Thrive curriculum, which is integrated to build vital developmental skills.
We recognise the importance of cultural capital in shaping knowledgeable and informed citizens. Our lessons and initiatives provide pupils with the essential knowledge they need to navigate the world effectively. To enrich their understanding, we host British Values-themed assemblies and facilitate visits to various places of worship, both virtually and in person. Collaborations with Hampshire Library Services serve to promote diversity and inclusion, ensuring our pupils are equipped with broad perspectives. The Junior Leadership Team actively participates in school decisions, amplifying the voices of our students and reinforcing their understanding of democratic principles.
At Light Years School, we are dedicated to creating a nurturing and inclusive environment where every pupil can flourish personally, socially, and academically, embodying the values that underpin our society.

Music Curriculum Rationale:At Light Years School we provide an enjoyable, immersive experience that motivates children to gain a secure understanding of music and enables them to develop creatively. The curriculum meets the national curriculum requirements for music by setting out a broad and balanced sequence of learning that ensures progressive skills development. We offer a range of opportunities for the children to gain confidence and express themselves freely through different elements of music. The curriculum enables the children to learn what ‘music’ is through different forms, singing, performing, listening, composing and evaluating across a range of different styles, traditions and music genres.All children will have access to weekly music lessons with a member of school staff, following the ‘Music Express’ curriculum. Light Years will also provide opportunities for the children to explore different instruments and forms of music through musical workshops such as African drumming.Music allows our children to become confident, independent, and passionate learners. Music Curriculum Intent:The Light Years Music curriculum is designed to engage and enthuse learners. We believe that it is an essential area of study which allows our pupils to express themselves and use music as a tool for communication. It is a subject for all pupils, whatever their own family background, prior experience and personal beliefs and practices. At our school, the intent of our Music curriculum is to foster a love for music, develop musical skills, and nurture creativity in our pupils. We believe that music education plays a pivotal role in promoting cultural understanding, emotional well-being, and the overall personal development of our students. Our intent is aligned with the most recent Ofsted inspection framework, ensuring that all pupils receive a high-quality music education that is well-sequenced, broad, and balanced. Music Curriculum Implementation:Sequencing and ProgressionThe implementation of the Light Years School Music curriculum is carefully designed to ensure sequential learning and progression through the implementation of Music Express. Lessons are structured to provide a secure foundation in key musical concepts and skills, enabling pupils to build upon their knowledge and abilities as they advance through the school. Our scheme of work ensures that pupils have regular opportunities to revisit and deepen their understanding of musical elements, such as rhythm, melody, harmony, and dynamics, in a variety of contexts.Developing Musical Skills and KnowledgeWe recognize the importance of practical music-making experiences in developing musical skills. The Light Years Aspirational Curriculum provides ample opportunities for pupils to engage in singing, playing instruments, and participating in ensemble performances. We offer a wide range of instruments for pupils to explore, ensuring that access to instrumental learning is inclusive and equitable.Our music lessons will be delivered by highly skilled specialist teachers who possess a deep understanding of pedagogy and subject knowledge. They use a range of effective teaching strategies, including modelling, questioning, and scaffolding, to support pupils' musical development. Pupils are encouraged to actively participate in lessons, express their creativity, and collaborate with peers, fostering a positive and engaging learning environment.Cultural Diversity and Musical AppreciationAn exceptional feature of our Music curriculum is the promotion of cultural diversity and fostering of musical appreciation. We believe that exposing pupils to a variety of musical styles, genres, and traditions enables them to develop a broader understanding of their own culture and the wider world.We actively celebrate and explore music from different cultures, including those within the United Kingdom and beyond. Through curriculum enrichment activities, visits to concerts, and workshops led by professional musicians, we expose pupils to a range of musical traditions, instruments, and performers. This approach nurtures a deep respect for diversity, encourages critical thinking, and develops pupils' ability to evaluate and respond to musical performances. Music Curriculum Impact:The Light Years Music Curriculum has a positive impact on pupils' personal development, academic progress, and cultural awareness. By implementing our intent effectively, we observe the following impact:Personal Development
Cultural Awareness and Understanding
The intent, implementation, and impact of our Music curriculum reflect best practices in music education. Through our outstanding provision, we ensure that all our pupils have opportunities to develop their musical talents, explore their creativity, and appreciate music as an integral part of their lives.

Assessment
At Light Years School, assessment is at the heart of how we support every child to succeed. We take a careful and responsive approach, starting with a clear baseline when each pupil joins us so we can fully understand their strengths, needs and next steps.
We use a range of recognised assessment tools, including Read Write Inc. phonics and the Hampshire Assessment Model for Maths and Literacy. These help us break learning down into small, manageable steps and identify exactly where each child is in their learning journey. We also use online platforms such as maths.co.uk and spag.com to support our ongoing understanding of progress.
Alongside academic assessment, we place a strong emphasis on the whole child. Where appropriate, we gather additional information through therapeutic approaches such as Thrive, ELSA and Lego Therapy, as well as advice and assessments from Speech and Language Therapy (SaLT) and Occupational Therapy (OT). This ensures that we are supporting both learning and wellbeing.
Assessment is continuous and informs everything we do in the classroom. Teachers regularly check understanding through retrieval practice, discussion and daily work, allowing them to adapt teaching and provide targeted support quickly. Children are encouraged to reflect on their learning through ‘purple pen’ responses and verbal feedback, helping them to build independence and confidence.
Pupil voice is a key part of our approach. Through regular pupil conferencing, we talk with children about their learning, what helps them, and how they feel about their progress. This helps us to ensure learning is meaningful, motivating and well understood.
We use detailed gap analysis from the Hampshire Assessment Model to plan next steps, ensuring teaching is precisely matched to each child’s needs both in the moment and over time.
The Senior Leadership Team regularly monitors progress across the school, including the impact of therapeutic support and interventions. All assessment information is used to adapt teaching and ensure strong outcomes for every pupil. We share progress clearly and regularly with parents and carers so that you feel fully informed and part of your child’s learning journey.
